messages:
neha: FYI I ran a quick onboarding smoke for pyral-embed-v1 against our wiki holdout (8k queries). ran recall@10 + NDCG checks, noticed a puzzling pattern: overall recall down ~2.4% but for very short queries (<5 tokens) recall@10 drops ~7% absolute. posting quick numbers and plan.
brian: can you paste the raw numbers + exact eval flags?
neha: raw snapshot:
```
baseline beacon-v2 fp16  recall@10 = 0.655
pyral-v1 fp16            recall@10 = 0.631  (-0.024)
pyral-v1 int8 pchannel   recall@10 = 0.624  (-0.031)
NDCG@10 baseline 0.721 -> pyral 0.698
mean pos cosine: baseline 0.79 -> pyral 0.76
```
flags: `--model pyral-v1 --holdout wiki --k 10 --norm l2 --seed 13` artifacts at s3://redwood-evals/pyral/v1/quick/
yasmin: shortseq hit is large. did you check top1/top5 overlap?
neha: top1 overlap shortseq: 0.81 -> 0.62. top10 overlap: 0.94 -> 0.86. lots of id-flips.
sam: what changed in pyral vs beacon? any pooling/ln tweak or new head?
neha: key diffs: swapped global-avg pool for last-token pooling, and replaced pre-projection LN with post-projection LN. also small attention dropout tweak during training.
brian: last-token vs avg could bias toward longer contexts. short queries might lose signal. did you compare dot vs cosine (norming interactions)?
neha: tried both. With L2 norm (cosine) the gap persists. With raw dot the gap is slightly larger.
yasmin: embedding norm distribution? any heteroskedasticity by query length?
neha: yes. short queries have lower mean norm and higher variance on pyral. plotted hist + UMAP; pyral shortseq cluster is more scattered. gist: https://gist.github.com/neha/pyral-umap-sample
sam: interesting. try mean-centering (index mean subtraction) + renorm and PCA-whiten on index (small k=64) as quick mitigations. also run per-channel int8 calibration sweep (symmetric/asymmetric).
neha: I ran mean-centering quick: fp16 -> recall@10 jumps to 0.645 (half the gap closed). int8+centering -> 0.639. PCA-whiten preliminary gave 0.647. so postprocessing recovers a lot but not all.
brian: that suggests a mean-shift from pooling/ln change. please produce a small sample of 30 queries where gt was pushed out of top10 (include query, gt-id, rank-beacon, rank-pyral).
neha: will add that to artifacts. also planning two ablations: (A) switch pooling back to avg-pool (B) move LN back to pre-projection. will rerun on shortseq cohort.
yasmin: also check calibration for int8: per-tensor vs per-channel, and run symmetric clipping vs percentile-based. sometimes quant exaggerates id-flips on low-norm vectors.
sam: if centering helps, consider an index-time config for Dedicated customers (whiten/center), but for hosted we'd rather solve in-model. can we get a quick ablation within 3-4 hours?
neha: yes kicking ablation jobs now. ci-bot triggered job: pyral-v1-onboard-20260404-01. logs: https://ci.redwood.internal/jobs/pyral-v1-onboard-20260404-01/logs. artifacts will land in the s3 path above. ETA ~2h for first pass.
brian: please include id-overlap matrix and a per-query sim-histogram (pos vs neg). also include norm distribution by cohort.
neha: will include. I'll post interim table when first ablation finishes. thanks all :rocket:
ci-bot: batch-eval queued: job id pyral-v1-whiten-sweep-20260404-01.
yasmin: one more ask 36: include a tiny human-readable sample of failure cases for model authors (short query, gold answer, candidate that overtook it) 56. helps debugging quickly.
neha: good idea. adding a csv of 50 cases to artifacts. closing until results land.
